qe: Which two districts in Bihar were the first to initiate the salt satyagraha, despite the state's landlocked geographical constraints making large-scale production impractical?
qh: बिहार के किन दो जिलों ने सबसे पहले नमक सत्याग्रह शुरू किया था, हालांकि राज्य की भौगोलिक सीमाओं के कारण यहाँ बड़े पैमाने पर नमक उत्पादन अव्यावहारिक था?
o: Champaran and Saran
Patna and Gaya
Munger and Bhagalpur
Muzaffarpur and Darbhanga
e: Detailed Explanation: Champaran and Saran were the pioneer districts in Bihar to launch the salt satyagraha. Since Bihar is landlocked and cannot produce salt efficiently, the act was largely symbolic, intended to demonstrate defiance of the colonial salt law.

qe: In Patna, which location was specifically selected as the site to manufacture salt in defiance of the British government’s salt laws?
qh: पटना में, ब्रिटिश सरकार के नमक कानूनों के उल्लंघन में नमक बनाने के लिए किस स्थान को विशेष रूप से चुना गया था?
o: Nakhas Pond
Dandi Beach
Sabarmati Bank
Ganga Ghat
e: Detailed Explanation: Nakhas Pond in Patna was chosen by local nationalist leaders, specifically under the guidance of Ambika Kant Sinha, as the symbolic site to manufacture salt and violate the colonial salt regulations.

qe: Following the salt satyagraha, which agitation gained rapid momentum in Bihar and replaced salt-making due to the latter's physical and geographical limitations?
qh: नमक सत्याग्रह के बाद, बिहार में कौन सा आंदोलन तेजी से आगे बढ़ा और नमक बनाने की प्रक्रिया के स्थान पर, अपनी भौगोलिक सीमाओं के कारण, प्रभावी हो गया?
o: No-chaukidari tax agitation
Anti-indigo revolt
Forest law violation movement
Railway workers' strike
e: Detailed Explanation: Because Bihar lacked coastal access for salt production, the movement quickly transitioned into the more practical and powerful 'no-chaukidari tax' agitation, which resonated more deeply with the rural agrarian population.

qe: In the Chhotanagpur tribal belt of Bihar, leaders Bonga Majhi and Somra Majhi led a movement that combined Gandhism with what specific socio-religious reform process?
qh: छोटानागपुर के आदिवासी बेल्ट में, बोंगा माझी और सोमरा माझी ने एक ऐसे आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया जिसने गांधीवाद को किस विशिष्ट सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधार प्रक्रिया के साथ जोड़ा?
o: Sanskritising lines
Western-liberal education
Industrial trade unionism
Puranic ritual revival
e: Detailed Explanation: Bonga Majhi and Somra Majhi led a movement in Hazaribagh that fused Gandhian ideals with 'sanskritising' efforts, urging followers to adopt khadi and renounce practices like meat-eating and liquor consumption to elevate their social status.

qe: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, signed in February 1931, placed the Congress on an equal footing with the colonial government. Which of the following was NOT part of the agreement?
qh: फरवरी 1931 में हस्ताक्षरित गांधी-इरविन समझौता, जिसने कांग्रेस को औपनिवेशिक सरकार के समकक्ष खड़ा कर दिया, में निम्नलिखित में से क्या समझौते का हिस्सा नहीं था?
o: Immediate public inquiry into police excesses
Release of political prisoners not convicted of violence
Right to make salt in coastal villages for personal consumption
Suspension of the civil disobedience movement
e: Detailed Explanation: While Irwin agreed to release prisoners, return seized lands, and allow salt-making for personal use, he flatly refused two of Gandhi's key demands: a public inquiry into police brutalities and the commutation of the death sentence for Bhagat Singh and his comrades.

qe: At the Karachi Congress session in 1931, two major resolutions were adopted that became the basic political and economic program of the Congress. What did the 'National Economic Programme' include?
qh: 1931 के कराची कांग्रेस सत्र में दो प्रमुख प्रस्ताव अपनाए गए जो कांग्रेस के बुनियादी राजनीतिक और आर्थिक कार्यक्रम बने। 'राष्ट्रीय आर्थिक कार्यक्रम' (National Economic Programme) में क्या शामिल था?
o: State ownership and control of key industries, mines, and transport
Mandatory taxation of all tax-free agrarian lands
The complete abolition of all local village panchayat judicial powers
The immediate merger of the Congress platform with the Aligarh school
e: Detailed Explanation: The Karachi Resolution on the National Economic Programme was revolutionary. It proposed state ownership/control of key industries, mines, and transport, along with provisions for a living wage, limited working hours, and the right to form unions.

qe: What was the significance of the resolution on 'Fundamental Rights' passed at the 1931 Karachi Congress session?
qh: 1931 के कराची कांग्रेस सत्र में पारित 'मौलिक अधिकारों' (Fundamental Rights) के प्रस्ताव का महत्व क्या था?
o: It guaranteed free speech, free press, universal adult franchise, and state neutrality in religious matters
It formally restricted the voting rights exclusively to wealthy aristocratic landowners
It established the British managing agencies as the ultimate authority over Indian education
It mandated the compulsory use of foreign textiles inside all public government offices
e: Detailed Explanation: The Karachi resolution provided the first blueprint of the rights Congress sought to guarantee in a free India, including universal adult franchise, equality before the law, freedom of speech/press, and secularism.

qe: Who officially opened the First Round Table Conference in London on November 12, 1930?
qh: 12 नवंबर, 1930 को लंदन में प्रथम गोलमेज सम्मेलन का औपचारिक उद्घाटन किसने किया था?
o: King George V
Ramsay MacDonald
Lord Irwin
Lord Willingdon
e: Detailed Explanation: The First Round Table Conference, the first major meeting between British and Indian representatives as equals, was officially opened by King George V on November 12, 1930.

qe: During the Second Round Table Conference, which representative was nominated by the Indian National Congress as its 'sole' delegate?
qh: द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन के दौरान, भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस द्वारा अपने 'एकमात्र' प्रतिनिधि के रूप में किसे नामित किया गया था?
o: Mahatma Gandhi
Madan Mohan Malaviya
Sarojini Naidu
Jawaharlal Nehru
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, the Congress agreed to participate in the second RTC, nominating Mahatma Gandhi as its sole official representative to negotiate with the British government.

qe: Why did Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference largely result in a deadlock regarding the constitutional question?
qh: द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन में गांधी की भागीदारी के परिणामस्वरूप संवैधानिक प्रश्न पर काफी हद तक गतिरोध क्यों उत्पन्न हुआ?
o: The session became deadlocked over the question of minorities and separate electorates for different communities
The British government explicitly refused to provide Gandhi with any accommodation in London
Gandhi demanded the immediate transfer of all British military power to the Maharaja of Patiala
The princely states completely resigned from the conference within the first hour of proceedings
e: Detailed Explanation: The conference failed to make progress because of the 'Minorities' Pact', where Muslims, depressed classes, Christians, and Anglo-Indians demanded separate electorates. Gandhi opposed this, arguing it would divide the nation, and refused to agree to any constitutional path conditional on solving this communal issue.

qe: Which of the following major announcements was made by Ramsay MacDonald at the conclusion of the Second Round Table Conference?
qh: द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन के समापन पर रामसे मैकडोनाल्ड (Ramsay MacDonald) द्वारा निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी बड़ी घोषणा की गई थी?
o: Setting up of three expert committees on finance, franchise, and states
The absolute declaration of India as an independent dominion status nation
The mandatory disbanding of all royal chambers and princely state councils
The immediate transfer of the Central Legislative Assembly to the city of Allahabad
e: Detailed Explanation: At the end of the second RTC, MacDonald announced the creation of two new Muslim-majority provinces (NWFP and Sindh), an Indian Consultative Committee, and three expert committees on finance, franchise, and states, while threatening a unilateral Communal Award if Indians failed to reach a consensus.

qe: What was the official British Government's justification for separating Burma from India in 1935?
qh: 1935 में बर्मा को भारत से अलग करने के लिए ब्रिटिश सरकार का आधिकारिक औचित्य क्या था?
o: Burma was not a natural part of the Indian subcontinent
The people of Burma demanded a merger with the Ottoman caliphate
The British Parliament failed to manage the maritime trade routes near Rangoon
The administrative cost of governing Burma exceeded the total revenue collection from Bihar
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission report and subsequent colonial planning formally recommended the separation of Burma from India, officially arguing that it was not a natural or integral part of the Indian subcontinent's socio-political geography.

qe: The 'Delhi Proposals' of 1927, which sought to bridge communal differences, demanded what representation for Muslims in the Central Legislative Assembly?
qh: 1927 के 'दिल्ली प्रस्तावों' (Delhi Proposals), जिन्होंने सांप्रदायिक मतभेदों को पाटने का प्रयास किया, ने केंद्रीय विधान सभा में मुसलमानों के लिए किस प्रतिनिधित्व की मांग की थी?
o: One-third representation
Fifty per cent representation
Ten per cent representation
Proportional to the total population of London
e: Detailed Explanation: The Delhi Proposals, which were later accepted by the Congress at Madras, demanded joint electorates with reserved seats and specifically asked for one-third of the seats in the Central Legislative Assembly to be reserved for Muslims.

qe: Which organization, originally floated by Nawab Salimullah of Dacca in 1906, was taken over by the group led by Agha Khan and Muhammad Shafi to preach loyalty to the empire?
qh: 1906 में ढाका के नवाब सलीमुल्लाह द्वारा मूल रूप से शुरू किए गए किस संगठन को आगा खान और मुहम्मद शफी के नेतृत्व वाले समूह द्वारा साम्राज्य के प्रति निष्ठा का उपदेश देने के लिए ले लिया गया था?
o: The All India Muslim League
The Sanatana Dharma Sabha
The British Indian Association
The All India Harijan Sangh
e: Detailed Explanation: The Muslim League was floated by Nawab Salimullah of Dacca in December 1906. It quickly came under the influence of the Agha Khan and Muhammad Shafi, aiming to maintain Muslim political loyalty to the British Empire while keeping the community away from the Congress.

qe: What was the significance of the Karachi Resolution's demand regarding 'state ownership'?
qh: कराची प्रस्ताव की 'राज्य स्वामित्व' (state ownership) के संबंध में मांग का क्या महत्व था?
o: It proposed state ownership and control of key industries, mines, and means of transport to end exploitation
It advocated for the absolute privatization of all primary school buildings in Bihar
It called for the direct handover of agricultural revenue to local village moneylenders
It mandated that all civil servants must be nominated by the European Managing Agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The Karachi Congress (1931) was the first time the party explicitly linked political freedom with economic liberation, proposing state ownership of key industrial and transport sectors to ensure that economic freedom for the 'starving millions' was a core political objective.

qe: Why did the younger nationalist section led by Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Bose object to the Nehru Report's preference for 'Dominion Status'?
qh: जवाहरलाल नेहरू और सुभाष चंद्र बोस के नेतृत्व वाले युवा राष्ट्रवादी गुट ने नेहरू रिपोर्ट में 'डोमिनियन स्टेटस' (Dominion Status) की प्राथमिकता पर आपत्ति क्यों जताई?
o: They demanded complete independence (Purna Swaraj) instead of the subordinate status offered by dominion membership
They believed that the report was secretly drafted by European managing agents
They were opposed to the linguistic reorganization of Indian provinces
They demanded that the central parliament should have 1000 members instead of 500
e: Detailed Explanation: The younger generation, increasingly radicalized, saw Dominion Status as a form of continued British tutelage. They refused to accept anything less than Purna Swaraj, leading to a major ideological clash within the Congress leadership.

qe: What did the Nehru Report propose regarding the linguistic reorganization of provinces?
qh: नेहरू रिपोर्ट ने प्रांतों के भाषाई पुनर्गठन के संबंध में क्या प्रस्ताव रखा था?
o: It recommended the formation of linguistic provinces
It rejected any regional division based on language, keeping old colonial boundaries
It suggested that all provinces should speak only English to promote unity
It proposed merging all provinces into a single uniform administrative block under a military Governor
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the key progressive recommendations of the 1928 Nehru Report was the advocacy for linguistic provinces, acknowledging the importance of regional languages in administrative and political organization.

qe: When discussing the federal structure, the Nehru Report proposed a central parliament. How was the House of Representatives to be elected?
qh: नेहरू रिपोर्ट के संघीय ढांचे पर चर्चा करते समय, एक केंद्रीय संसद का प्रस्ताव रखा गया था। प्रतिनिधि सभा (House of Representatives) का चुनाव कैसे किया जाना था?
o: Elected on the basis of adult suffrage
Nominated entirely by the princely rulers
Elected exclusively by the members of the colonial civil services
Appointed by the High Court judges based on technical competence
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report proposed a robust democratic structure. The House of Representatives was to have 500 members, all elected directly by the people based on the principle of adult suffrage, representing a revolutionary move for the time.

qe: What was the significance of the 'Meerut Conspiracy Case' (March 1929) in the political history of India during the Civil Disobedience era?
qh: सविनय अवज्ञा युग के दौरान भारत के राजनीतिक इतिहास में 'मेरठ षड्यंत्र मामला' (मार्च 1929) का क्या महत्व था?
o: It was a crackdown by the government on labor leaders and socialists to suppress the growth of trade unions
It resulted in the immediate liberation of all indentured labor working in the tea gardens of Assam
It allowed the formation of a formal alliance between the Muslim League and the Congress
It mandated the immediate payment of a living wage to all industrial workers in Bombay
e: Detailed Explanation: The Meerut Conspiracy Case was a major state action aimed at crippling the nascent socialist and communist movement. The government arrested prominent labor union leaders, unionists, and socialist thinkers, attempting to prevent the working class from becoming an independent political force.

qe: What was the significance of the 1930 Civil Disobedience Movement's approach to law-breaking compared to the earlier Non-Cooperation Movement?
qh: 1930 के सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन (Civil Disobedience Movement) के कानून तोड़ने के दृष्टिकोण का शुरुआती असहयोग आंदोलन की तुलना में क्या महत्व था?
o: It explicitly involved the violation of law from the very beginning, unlike simple non-cooperation with foreign rule
It relied purely on the legal petitioning methods approved by the High Courts
It was limited strictly to boycotting foreign cloth and ignored salt taxes
It prohibited the participation of women in all public processions and street protests
e: Detailed Explanation: While the Non-Cooperation Movement was based on withdrawing support (non-cooperation), the Civil Disobedience Movement marked a shift to active defiance, where participants explicitly violated specific colonial laws (like the salt law) as a symbol of rejecting British sovereignty.

qe: Which of the following was a primary reason for the large-scale participation of business groups in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
qh: सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन में व्यापारिक समूहों की बड़े पैमाने पर भागीदारी का एक प्राथमिक कारण निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा था?
o: They had benefited from the nationalist emphasis on swadeshi and faced increasing competition from British imports
They were legally required by the colonial state to donate all factory profits to the Congress
They were excluded from the legislative council seats and wanted to protest against the Viceroy
They sought to organize a permanent army of private guards to protect their maritime assets
e: Detailed Explanation: The business class, particularly textile manufacturers, supported the movement because the boycott of foreign goods provided a protected domestic market for their produce, shielding them from the unfair competitive advantage enjoyed by British imports.

qe: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, how did the response of the Muslim community compare to their participation in the Non-Cooperation Movement?
qh: सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन के दौरान, मुस्लिम समुदाय की प्रतिक्रिया उनके असहयोग आंदोलन में भागीदारी की तुलना में कैसी थी?
o: Muslim participation was nowhere near the level of the Non-Cooperation Movement
It was exponentially higher due to the immediate promise of separate electorates
It remained exactly the same as the 1920-22 levels
They completely withdrew from all political activity after the 1930 report was published
e: Detailed Explanation: Muslim participation in the 1930 movement did not reach the unprecedented heights seen in 1920–22. The lack of a shared religious platform (like the Khilafat) and the deepening communal politics meant their participation was relatively limited.

qe: Why was the 1931 Karachi Congress session considered particularly memorable in the history of the Indian freedom struggle?
qh: 1931 का कराची कांग्रेस सत्र भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के इतिहास में विशेष रूप से यादगार क्यों माना जाता है?
o: It adopted landmark resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme
It passed a formal resolution declaring the immediate and permanent merger of all princely states
It announced the total legal abolition of the central Imperial Legislative Council benches
It was the only session presided over by a representative of the British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1931 Karachi session is historic because it formally endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and, more importantly, adopted two seminal resolutions: on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme, which defined the Congress's vision for a just, post-independence India.

qe: What was the official justification provided by the British colonial government to justify the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency?
qh: बंबई प्रेसीडेंसी से सिंध को अलग करने के लिए ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक सरकार द्वारा प्रदान किया गया आधिकारिक औचित्य क्या था?
o: Administrative and linguistic distinctiveness
The total structural collapse of the local maritime shipping routes
The immediate demand for land revenue exemptions by the wealthy landlords of Sindh
To exclusively favor the industrial growth of the British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: Based on the Simon Commission's recommendations, the government decided to separate Sindh from the Bombay Presidency, justifying it primarily on the basis of its unique linguistic and administrative needs as an independent unit.

qe: How did the 1935 Act affect the taxation demarcation between provincial and local municipal finance, which had been in practice since the reforms of 1919?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय और स्थानीय नगरपालिका वित्त के बीच उस कराधान सीमा (taxation demarcation) को कैसे प्रभावित किया, जो 1919 के सुधारों के बाद से अभ्यास में थी?
o: The demarcation of taxation was scrapped, allowing provinces to consolidate finance and empower local bodies
It imposed a mandatory flat-rate tax on all village panchayats nationally
It required local bodies to transfer all tax revenues directly to the British Treasury in London
It established an independent high court bench to manage the tax assessment of every town
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Government of India Act scrapped the strict 1919 demarcation between provincial and local taxes, intending to provide more flexibility. However, while it aimed to empower ministries, in practice, provincial governments often restricted the taxation powers of local municipal institutions.

qe: Which historical incident occurred just six days before the Karachi session (March 1931) of the Congress, leading to black flag demonstrations against Gandhi's route?
qh: कांग्रेस के कराची सत्र (मार्च 1931) से ठीक छह दिन पहले कौन सी ऐतिहासिक घटना घटी थी, जिसके कारण गांधी के रास्ते में काले झंडे का विरोध प्रदर्शन हुआ था?
o: The execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru
The assassination of Michael O'Dwyer by Udham Singh
The arrest of the Ali brothers for organizing industrial strikes
The burning of the Ferozshah Kotla assembly building
e: Detailed Explanation: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were executed on March 23, 1931. As Gandhi traveled to Karachi for the Congress session on March 29, many youth activists, disillusioned that Gandhi hadn't secured a commutation of their death sentences, greeted him with black flags in protest.

qe: Despite participating in the Civil Disobedience Movement, many big business groups remained skeptical. What was their primary underlying fear regarding the mobilization of factory labor?
qh: सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन में भाग लेने के बावजूद, कई बड़े व्यावसायिक समूह संशय में रहे। फैक्ट्री श्रम की लामबंदी के संबंध में उनका प्राथमिक अंतर्निहित डर क्या था?
o: They feared that the movement could spiral into labor unrest and strikes inside their own factories
They were afraid that the Congress would nationalize their maritime shipping assets instantly
They worried that their bank deposits would be transferred to the Tilak Swaraj Fund
They believed that the government would legally seize their private property for the public welfare
e: Detailed Explanation: While business groups supported the boycott of foreign goods, they remained deeply wary of the broader mass movement. They feared that the Congress's radical call for mass action could destabilize their own industrial operations and trigger unpredictable labor strikes inside their factories.

qe: The 'No-Changers' successfully utilized the quiet phase after the suspension of the movement to organize 'Ward Committees'. What was the primary purpose of these ward-level organizations?
qh: नो-चेंजर्स ने आंदोलन के निलंबन के बाद शांत चरण का उपयोग 'वार्ड समितियों' (Ward Committees) को व्यवस्थित करने के लिए किया। इन वार्ड-स्तरीय संगठनों का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To serve as the organizational backbone for future mass struggle and execute constructive village work
To directly manage the currency exchange tracking rates inside the city municipality boards
To lobby the British Parliament for direct nominations into the Imperial Legislative Council
To serve as military training centers for organizing armed raids against coastal salt works
e: Detailed Explanation: The ward committees formed part of the structural effort to keep the movement alive during the quiet phase. They organized constructive tasks like teaching spinning, educating the illiterate, and managing disaster relief, ensuring the party remained entrenched at the grass-roots level.

qe: Why was the 1930 Civil Disobedience Movement significantly different from the Non-Cooperation Movement regarding the participation of different social sections?
qh: 1930 का सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन सामाजिक वर्गों की भागीदारी के संबंध में असहयोग आंदोलन से काफी अलग क्यों था?
o: Mass participation of peasants and business groups compensated for the decline in participation of some elite urban intelligentsia groups
The movement completely barred the participation of all urban middle classes and students
Muslim participation in the 1930 movement was higher than in the 1920-22 phase
It restricted all protest activity to the maritime ports managed by British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: While the participation of urban professionals (lawyers, students) declined compared to 1920, the Civil Disobedience Movement gained massive strength from the deep involvement of the peasantry and the business community, which effectively compensated for the drop in other areas.

qe: A logistical supply route maps out a right-angled triangular course from central base O. A transport vehicle travels 28 km North, and then shifts orientation to move 21 km East to reach checkpoint S. Find the absolute straight-line distance from O to S.
qh: एक परिवहन वाहन केंद्रीय बेस O से 28 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 21 किमी जाकर चेकपॉइंट S पर पहुँचता है। O से S की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 35 km
49 km
42 km
38 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial path forms a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of 28 km and 21 km. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{28^2 + 21^2} = \sqrt{784 + 441} = \sqrt{1225} = \mathbf{35\text{ km}}$.

qe: In an ecosystem biological survey mapping energy flow metrics, if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of a tropical biome is 40,000 units and the energy lost during metabolic plant respiration (R) is 25,000 units, calculate the total Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).
qh: ऊर्जा प्रवाह मापदंडों का मानचित्रण करने वाले एक पारिस्थितिकी जैविक सर्वेक्षण में, यदि एक उष्णकटिबंधीय बायोम की शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) 40,000 इकाइयाँ है और पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा 25,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो कुल सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) की गणना करें।
o: 65,000 units
15,000 units
40,000 units
50,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the foundational ecological productivity balance formula: $NPP = GPP - R$, we rewrite to isolate Gross Primary Productivity: $GPP = NPP + R$.
Substituting the values: $GPP = 40,000 + 25,000 = \mathbf{65,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: Which prominent leader presided over the special session of the Indian National Congress in 1918 that rejected the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals as 'disappointing'?
qh: 1918 में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के उस विशेष सत्र की अध्यक्षता किसने की थी जिसने मोंटेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड प्रस्तावों को 'निराशाजनक' बताकर खारिज कर दिया था?
o: Hasan Imam
Ambika Charan Majumdar
Dadabhai Naoroji
W.C. Bonnerjee
e: Detailed Explanation: The special session of the Congress held in Bombay in August 1918, which formally evaluated and rejected the Montagu-Chelmsford reform proposals, was presided over by Hasan Imam.

qe: The historic 1928 Nehru Report drafted a constitution that proposed which legislative structure for the central government?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट ने एक संविधान का मसौदा तैयार किया जिसने केंद्र सरकार के लिए कौन सी विधायी संरचना प्रस्तावित की थी?
o: A bicameral parliament consisting of a 500-member House of Representatives and a 200-member Senate
A unicameral Imperial Assembly with members nominated solely by the provincial Governors
A system managed entirely by executive councillors with no legislative chamber
A chamber featuring 72 members elected strictly by the regional mercantile chambers
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report proposed a sophisticated bicameral parliament: a lower house (House of Representatives) of 500 members elected by universal adult franchise and an upper house (Senate) of 200 members elected by provincial councils, establishing the framework for a democratic central legislature.

qe: What specific provision in the 1928 Nehru Report addressed the protection of religious and cultural minorities?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट में धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक अल्पसंख्यकों की सुरक्षा के संबंध में किस विशिष्ट प्रावधान को संबोधित किया गया था?
o: Full protection to cultural and religious interests of Muslims and other minorities
The mandatory requirement that all religious schools be managed by British military tribunals
The total abolition of any protection for regional linguistic groups
Granting exclusive legislative veto powers to the High Court judges
e: Detailed Explanation: Recognizing the necessity of minority trust, the report included explicit guarantees for the full protection of the cultural and religious interests of all minorities, including the Muslims, in any future constitutional framework.

qe: Which of the following was a structural achievement of the Swarajists inside the legislative chambers during their period of parliamentary activity?
qh: विधायी कक्षों में अपने संसदीय गतिविधि के चरण के दौरान स्वराजवादियों की कौन सी संरचनात्मक उपलब्धि थी?
o: The defeat of the Public Safety Bill in 1928
The complete physical destruction of the central Imperial Legislative Council building
The mandatory recruitment of all swadeshi textile factory workers into the provincial councils
The direct legal transfer of the Viceroy's executive council power to the Indian League front
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the most noteworthy achievements of the Swarajists in the Central Legislative Assembly was the defeat of the Public Safety Bill in 1928, which the government aimed to use to deport foreign activists and suppress the spread of socialist ideology.
